openTomorrow: Yes, absolutely. I need to set up that group challenge for my 8 clients. This app makes it easy to create and track multiple people at once, which is exactly what I need for my training program.
secured: I think it means the challenge data is protected and safe - like my clients' progress and personal information won't be shared or lost. Security for the challenge details.
freeze: My guess is it's a way to pause a challenge temporarily without deleting it. If someone gets injured or needs a break, I can freeze their challenge and restart later without losing their progress.
selfReported: That's when participants log their own results and check-ins instead of me tracking everything for them. It puts accountability on my clients to be honest about whether they completed the workout.
best: Seeing that 'Looks good' confirmation on the challenge I created. It validated that my goal - workout 5 times weekly for 7 days - was solid and realistic for what I want to implement with my clients.
worst: Having to select categories individually. I wish there was an option to tag multiple categories at once. Fitness is the obvious choice for my clients, but I'd love to also include Discipline to reinforce the mental aspect.
tellFriend: Yeah, I'd tell other trainers about this. I'd say it's a clean app for setting up group challenges - really streamlined for creating accountability. Perfect for tracking multiple clients on the same goal without micromanaging everything manually.
